clue.text: Rising operettist excising an intestinal growth

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the remaining letters are read from bottom to top
excising means cutting out, so the word an is removed from the composer's name

parts.note: Arthur Sullivan composed the Gilbert and Sullivan operettas

explanation.surface: A composer of comic operas is having a growth removed from his gut.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking AN out of SULLIVAN leaves SULLIV, and 'Rising' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A villus is one of the tiny finger-like projections lining the small intestine.

clue.text: They expose limbs, given sweets — is drink included?

indicators.note: included means the following pieces go inside the word for the sweets

parts.note: mints are sweets
kir is a drink of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the sweets and drinks come with an outfit that shows a lot of leg.
explanation.walkthrough: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine with blackcurrant liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Short skirts leave the legs, the limbs, on show.

clue.text: Womaniser reluctant to go to a South American city …

parts.note: loth is an old spelling of loath, reluctant
Rio de Janeiro in Brazil

explanation.surface: A philanderer is unwilling to travel to Brazil.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, a seducer in a Restoration play, became a byword for a rake.

clue.text: Senior officer I covered with dirt-like slimy stuff

indicators.note: covered with means the officer and I sit inside the word for dirt

parts.note: mud is wet dirt
CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: A commanding officer finds himself plastered in slime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirt-like' reads as one word, but the definition starts at 'like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucoid means resembling mucus, the slimy secretion.

clue.text: … or mental (crazy) North American one

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of or and mental are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: It continues the previous clue: the womaniser goes to Rio, or else to a mad city in North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'city' in 3 down, so this means a North American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Montreal is a large city in Quebec, Canada.

clue.text: Gap between outstanding features of holiday mostly in prison

indicators.note: in places the shortened holiday inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a prison

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: leave is time off, a holiday

explanation.surface: A prisoner considers the gap between the high points of a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'outstanding features' are breasts, not highlights of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleavage is the hollow between a woman's breasts, cheekily called prominent features.

clue.text: Hybrid child receiving letter from Athens

indicators.note: receiving means the child word takes the Greek letter inside it

parts.note: a minor is a child in law
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A mixed-race child gets a letter from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur of Greek myth was half man, half bull, a crossbred monster.

clue.text: A vote for German 10, or Greek hero

parts.note: ja is German for yes, a vote in favour
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone votes for a German footballer wearing the number 10 shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a mighty warrior on the Greek side in the Trojan War.

clue.text: Dance to cast a lustful eye over

indicators.note: over says the word is turned over, read backwards up the column

parts.note: to leer is to look lustfully

explanation.surface: Someone at a dance eyes up a partner lecherously.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish country dance.

clue.text: Want the French to be annoying

parts.note: to want is to need
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Desire for French things becomes irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate them, so it means being annoying to them.

clue.text: Is like "running water", infiltrating bogus food item

indicators.note: infiltrating means those pieces get inside the word for bogus

parts.note: bogus means fake
H and C, hot and cold, are the taps of running water in old hotel guides

explanation.surface: A fraudster claims his product resembles a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British guidebooks listed rooms with 'h & c', hot and cold running water; 'like' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishcake is a patty of fish and potato, fried.

clue.text: Musician to make off with most of capital

parts.note: to ravish is, in an old sense, to carry off by force

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the city is dropped

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey

explanation.surface: A musician plans to steal most of the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravi Shankar was the celebrated Indian sitar player.

clue.text: Colourless church with scent outside

indicators.note: outside means the scented word goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: aromatic means having a scent

explanation.surface: A drab church filled with incense.
explanation.definitionFit: Achromatic describes something without hue, having no colour.

clue.text: Work hard to penetrate punctuation mark by which publisher may be recognised

definitions.text: by which publisher may be recognised

indicators.note: to penetrate means work and hard get inside the punctuation mark

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
op is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An editor labours over a punctuation mark that marks the publisher's identity.
explanation.walkthrough: OP and H go into COLON: COL-OPH-ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A colophon is a publisher's emblem or imprint, the logo on a book's spine.

clue.text: Radish top getting into cooking vessel results in severe cold

indicators.note: getting into means the first letter goes inside the cooking pot word

parts.note: a steamer is a pot for steaming food

indicators.note: top in a down clue means the first letter

explanation.surface: A radish falls into a steaming pan, with chilly consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the top of Radish, goes into STEAMER: ST-R-EAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a heavy head cold, one that makes the nose run freely.

clue.text: Not beginning to flag pain

indicators.note: not beginning means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to flag is to languish, to droop

explanation.surface: Someone vows not to start tiring as the hurt sets in.
explanation.definitionFit: Anguish is severe mental or physical suffering.

clue.text: Pause for popular insect with no bottom

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a termite is an insect

explanation.surface: A trendy bug without a bottom takes a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to stop for a time, suspend.

clue.text: Get rid of bouncer and hawker

parts.note: a roo, kangaroo, bounces along
a tout sells tickets

explanation.surface: A nightclub wants rid of its doorman and a street trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncer' looks like a doorman but is a hopping kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out is to eradicate, dig up and remove.

clue.text: Time to wake up, accepting Flynn's cross-dressing persona

indicators.note: accepting means the actor's first name goes inside the waking word

parts.note: to rouse is to wake up
Errol Flynn was a Hollywood star

explanation.surface: An actor is roused to play a part in drag.
explanation.walkthrough: Errol Flynn was a swashbuckling Hollywood actor of the 1930s and 40s.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeches part, in which a woman plays a male character in theatre or opera.

clue.text: I adore getting drunk with member of band's crew

indicators.note: getting drunk says the letters of i adore reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A fan gets drunk with the stagehands at a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie sets up and transports the equipment for a touring band.

clue.text: Old friends bringing equipment to hospital

parts.note: kit is gear, equipment
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Friends bring gear into a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Kith is an archaic word for one's acquaintances, as in kith and kin.

clue.text: Aquatic animal losing month's work

indicators.note: losing means the abbreviated month is taken away

parts.note: an octopus is a sea creature
Oct is short for October

explanation.surface: A sea creature loses a month's labour.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a composition, a creative work.

clue.text: Put at risk, adopting a system of measurement

indicators.note: adopting means the word for endangering takes the letter a in

parts.note: to imperil something is to endanger it, put it at risk

explanation.surface: A dangerous move to switch to a new way of measuring.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperial system uses feet, pounds and pints rather than metric units.

clue.text: Half of hair lotion put around part of London

indicators.note: put around means the lotion word is wrapped round the half

parts.note: balm is a soothing ointment

indicators.note: half of means the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: A hair product applied in a London district.
explanation.definitionFit: Balham is a district of south London.

clue.text: Very devout, hot and reportedly sour

parts.note: H is the tap abbreviation for hot

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for sour is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: acidic means sour

explanation.surface: A pious person is said to be both hot-tempered and bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasidic Judaism is a strictly observant, ultra-orthodox movement.

clue.text: Socialist revolutionary eating pub lunch

indicators.note: eating means the socialist word swallows the pub
revolutionary means the word is turned round

parts.note: red is a socialist
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A left-wing radical tucks into a pub meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunch' seems wrong for this meal, but in much of Britain the midday meal is called that.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern England and many schools the midday meal is still called dinner.
